prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1183; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The injury does not fit the crash: the impact was very light, yet the claimed injury is severe.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Parking lot collision reported by the insured driver, who is named on the policy. Vehicle damage appears consistent with the described low-speed contact at the rear bumper.

Entry 2: Police attended the scene and confirmed the claimant was present in the vehicle at the time. Photos taken at the scene show the damage and the general layout of the lot.

Entry 3: Claimant has reported a knee injury and is now represented by counsel. All further contact is to go through the attorney's office.

Entry 4: No independent witnesses have come forward. The only accounts on file are from the claimant and the insured driver.

Entry 5: Checked prior claims history. No earlier damage to the vehicle is recorded, and nothing suggests the damage predates the coverage start.

Entry 6: Attorney's demand package received, describing ongoing knee treatment. Medical records requested to review the diagnosis and treatment course.

Entry 7: Medical records show an initial evaluation followed by a standard course of physiotherapy. Improvement was noted at each follow-up visit and the frequency of treatment reduced over time.

Entry 8: Records reviewed and no prior injury or complaint involving the same knee is noted in the claimant's history. The severity of the reported injury still seems high for an impact of this force.

Entry 9: Claimant's recorded account has changed slightly since the first interview, with a few added details about the moment of impact. The core description of the event remains the same.

Entry 10: Medical opinion requested from the review nurse on whether the injury matches the mechanism described. Response indicates the treatment was appropriate but the link between the impact and the severity of the injury needs further review.

Entry 11: File referred for further review pending the medical opinion and attorney correspondence. No payment decision has been made at this stage.
